title: Streaming chat: handoff API & graceful backpressure patterns for Python SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a developer-friendly streaming 'handoff' primitive for Python SDK that makes it easy to route streaming chat events to multiple consumers (sync/async), support graceful backpressure, and enable resumable consumption checkpoints. Scope includes API design, a reference implementation, unit + integration tests, and migration notes for existing stream iterator users. Non-goals: redesigning TypeScript/Go SDKs (tracked separately), adding new server-side runtime features.
acceptance_criteria: Public API with a minimal surface that supports both sync and async consumers without separate code paths
Backpressure control that prevents unbounded memory growth under slow consumers and provides signals for latency-sensitive apps
Resumability: ability to checkpoint a stream position and resume within the same model session or fall back to non-resumable mode when server doesn't support it
Comprehensive unit tests and an integration test against staging stream endpoint
Benchmark showing <10% median latency regression for common short-response workloads compared to current iterator baseline when backpressure disabled
test_plan: Unit tests for event demultiplexer, ack/commit semantics, and buffer eviction policies
Integration tests using local stream-faker that emits mix of deltas, tokens, and control events; simulate slow consumer to assert backpressure throttling
E2E demo app in examples/stream-handoff that wires a sync handler and an async analytics sink
Performance benchmark: run 10k short responses and record p50/p95 latency and memory usage with/without backpressure enabled
description_details: API proposal (summary): introduce StreamHandoff context manager returned by client.stream_handoff(...). The object exposes: .events() iterator (sync), .aevents() async iterator, .ack(event_id) to allow consumer-driven checkpointing, and .drain(timeout) for graceful shutdown.

Backpressure model: token-bucket with configurable window_size (number of in-flight events allowed) and 'drop_policy' options (block | buffer | drop-oldest). Default is block with configurable timeout to keep ergonomics for low-latency apps.

Resumability: when server includes resume_cursor we persist cursor on ack; if session lost, client attempts resume by sending last cursor. If resume fails, API surfaces RecoverableResumeError for caller to decide fallback.
Telemetry hooks: expose event-level hooks for tracing (trace_id header passthrough), metrics for buffered_events, dropped_events, resume_attempts; wire into console tracing.

Trade-offs considered: Simple iterator-only design is easiest for users but lacks multi-consumer support. Full actor/queue model increases complexity. Chosen handoff primitive aims for middle ground: single source of truth with lightweight adapters for sync/async consumers.
Compatibility: provide a compatibility shim that exposes old .stream() iterator signature backed by the handoff primitive so existing customers see minimal changes.

Security: no additional secrets required; resume cursor treated as opaque token stored in-memory by default. For Private deployments with long-lived cursors we will document KMS storage patterns in follow-ups.
Non-functional constraints: memory cap default 32MB per stream; when hit, handoff switches to drop-oldest unless user opts to block and tune timeouts.

Open question: default drop policy — team discussion leaned towards block-with-timeout to avoid surprise data loss, but we need legal/PM confirmation for default behavior for high-throughput customers.
Migration notes: examples/compatibility.md added in repo showing 3-line migration to handoff API. Will include release notes under sdk-py-2.4.0.
